newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish mixed, June T-bond sags.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish mixed, June T-bond sags.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended the session mixed with June T-bonds lower after lethargic trade heading into the long U.S. Memorial Day weekend.
Debt futures close early Friday and are shut Monday.
June Treasury bonds sagged as low as 108-30/32 in morning action, hampered by heavy sales from a variety of firms.
At 1300 CDT/1800 GMT, June rallied slightly after the minutes from the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting were released, but couldn't muster any followthrough.
June drifted back near session lows again late on quiet volume, traders said.
The minutes showed that FOMC members voted unanimously at the March 25 meeting to raise rates by a quarter percentage point, and a few policy makers wanted a bigger increase.
The policy group also voted unanimously to adopt a so-called symmetric directive that did not bias policy toward either tightening or loosening during the period leading up to the May 20 meeting.
"The minutes gave us a little bit of a bid," a T-bond futures trader said. "It seems there was no presumption toward further tightening and a switch toward a more neutral directive," the trader said.
Still, debt futures held those gains only briefly before turning mixed again.
"They traded it up and tried to rally it, but it didn't work out the way the bulls planned," a Euro trader said. "We're done for the week."
Much of the morning trading was directionless, with traders eyeing key 108-29/32, the seven-percent cash yield equivalent.
One technician put June T-bond support at 108-24/32. Another said 108-16/32 to 18/32 was important, and said a move through there would push June to 108-12/32.
June bumped up against resistance at 109-12/32 several times but failed to pop above there. Traders noted the overall slim size of Thursday's range.
Early in the session, traders reported scant impact from the latest weekly jobless claims, which rose to 322,000 in the May 17 week after a revised 317,000 in the previous week.

At the close, June T-bonds were down 7/32 at 109-02/32, 10-year notes were down 4/32 at 107-01/32, muni bonds were up 4/32 at 116-10/32, Sept T-bills were flat at 94.550, and December Eurodollars fell 0.025 to 93.710.
